title: Unit 2: Differentiation: Definition and Fundamental Properties

topics.name: The definition of the derivative
covers: Defining the derivative of a function at a point and as a function

topics.name: Derivatives of elementary functions and differentiation rules

guide.title: Differentiation: definition and fundamental properties: review guide
guide.intro: The derivative is the instantaneous rate of change: the limit of average rates of change. This unit defines it, connects it to continuity, and builds the rules for differentiating sums, products, quotients, and elementary functions.

sections.title: The definition of the derivative
body: f′(a) = lim h→0 (f(a + h) − f(a))/h: the slope of the tangent line at x = a, and the instantaneous rate of change. As a function, f′(x) uses the same limit at every x.
A difference quotient computed from a table or graph estimates the derivative. A symmetric difference, (f(a + h) − f(a − h))/(2h), is usually the better estimate.
points: Recognize a limit as a derivative in disguise: lim h→0 ((2 + h)³ − 8)/h is f′(2) for f(x) = x³.
The derivative's units are output units per input unit.

sections.title: Differentiability and continuity
body: If f is differentiable at a, it is continuous at a. The converse fails: a function can be continuous but not differentiable at a corner, a cusp, or a vertical tangent.
To make a piecewise function differentiable at a break point, make it continuous there (values match) and make the one-sided derivatives match (slopes match).
points: |x| is continuous but not differentiable at 0 (a corner).
A jump or a hole rules out differentiability.
Check the values first, then the slopes.

sections.title: Differentiation rules
body: Power rule: d/dx xⁿ = nxⁿ⁻¹. Constant multiples and sums differentiate term by term. Product rule: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′. Quotient rule: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v².
Elementary derivatives: (sin x)′ = cos x, (cos x)′ = −sin x, (tan x)′ = sec²x, (eˣ)′ = eˣ, (ln x)′ = 1/x, (aˣ)′ = aˣ ln a.
points: Tangent line at x = a: y = f(a) + f′(a)(x − a).
Simplify before differentiating when you can.
The quotient rule's numerator starts with u′v (“low d-high minus high d-low”).

example.prompt: Find the equation of the line tangent to f(x) = x² eˣ at x = 1.
example.solution: f′(x) = 2x eˣ + x² eˣ = eˣ(x² + 2x), so f′(1) = 3e and f(1) = e. The tangent line is y = e + 3e(x − 1), or y = 3ex − 2e.

misconceptions: Corners, cusps, and vertical tangents are continuous but not differentiable.
The product rule is u′v + uv′.
“The derivative at a point is the average rate of change.”
It is the limit of average rates as the interval shrinks to zero.
The power rule doesn't apply to exponentials; d/dx eˣ = eˣ.

questions.prompt: A differentiable function has f(1.9) = 3.61 and f(2.1) = 4.41. Using these values, what is the best estimate of f′(2)?
questions.explanation: Use the symmetric difference quotient: (f(2.1) − f(1.9))/(2.1 − 1.9) = 0.80/0.20 = 4.0.
choiceExplanations: 8.0 divides 0.80 by 0.10, the half-width, instead of the full width 0.20.
0.80 is the change in f, not divided by the change in x.
2.0 is the x-value, not the derivative.

questions.explanation: The graph has no break at x = 1, so f is continuous. It has a corner there: the slope is −1 on the left and +1 on the right, so f′(1) doesn't exist.
choiceExplanations: There is no break in the graph, so f is continuous.
Differentiability always implies continuity, so this combination is impossible.
The left and right slopes disagree, so there is no derivative at the corner.

questions.prompt: Let f(x) = ax² + b for x ≤ 1 and f(x) = 4x − 1 for x > 1. For which values of a and b is f differentiable at x = 1?
questions.explanation: Continuity: a + b = 4(1) − 1 = 3. Matching slopes: 2a(1) = 4, so a = 2. Then b = 3 − 2 = 1.
choiceExplanations: a = 4 matches the slope as if the left piece's derivative were a, not 2ax.
a = 1, b = 2 makes f continuous, but the left slope is 2, not 4.
b = 3 makes a + b = 5, so f would jump at x = 1.

questions.explanation: Quotient rule: ((sin x)′ · x − sin x · (x)′)/x² = (x cos x − sin x)/x².
choiceExplanations: The quotient rule subtracts the two terms; it doesn't add them.
cos x divides the derivatives, which isn't the quotient rule.
This reverses the order of subtraction in the numerator.

questions.prompt: What is the equation of the line tangent to y = ln x at x = e?
questions.explanation: At x = e, y = ln e = 1 and the slope is 1/e. So y − 1 = (1/e)(x − e), which simplifies to y = x/e.
choiceExplanations: y = ex − e² + 1 uses slope e, the reciprocal of the correct slope.
y = x − e + 1 uses slope 1 instead of 1/e.
y = x/e + 1 doesn't pass through (e, 1); it adds the y-value without subtracting (1/e)e.
